Source step. On the staged payload, the map-walk has reached the `TAG_ID` branch and `pairs[i].value` is the 48-byte CBOR text value. `fu_coswid_read_string()` duplicates all 48 bytes, preserving the embedded NUL after the prefix `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`.

The parsed text from step 1 is stored as a C string. Because `g_strdup` stops at the first NUL byte, `priv->id` becomes the exact 36-byte prefix `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`; the later padding bytes do not survive.
During serialization the stored ID from step 2 is non-NULL, so the writer attempts GUID conversion on it before considering the plain-string fallback.
The string passed from step 3 is 36 bytes long because of step 2's NUL truncation, so this top-level format rejection is not taken and the malformed value is treated as a candidate GUID.

The candidate GUID is split into five heap strings with lengths `[8, 4, 7, 8, 5]`: `00002800`, `0000`, `0002800`, `00002800`, `00000`. The last token `split[4]` is a 6-byte allocation including its terminator, matching the ASan allocation stack from `g_strsplit`.

Root-cause step. Only `split[2]`, `split[3]`, and `split[4]` are malformed, so the `&&` chain evaluates false as soon as `split[0]` and `split[1]` match `8` and `4`. The function therefore fails to reject the `8-4-7-8-5` layout. The later `g_ascii_string_to_unsigned` calls on `split[0..3]` still succeed because those tokens are valid hex within the permitted numeric ranges, so control reaches the final tail-field loop.

The tail parser is hard-coded for six 2-byte chunks, i.e. a 12-hex-digit `split[4]`. With step 5's 5-character last field, iteration `i == 3` derives the source pointer `split[4] + 6`, which is the one-past-the-end pointer of the 6-byte allocation `"00000\0"`.

Sink. When step 7 reaches `i == 3`, this exact copy reads 2 bytes starting at `split[4] + 6`, immediately past the heap object for the last GUID field. The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this line and names `g_strsplit` / `g_strdup` as the allocation path.
